notes:
Summary: Cascade Support Grid is a mid-to-large contact center platform provider that ships agent-assist + ticket summarization to 300+ enterprise customers. Primary pain: unpredictable spikes (product launches, Black Friday, outage cascades) that cause long agent wait times and throttled model access. Current setup: hybrid — core tenant data on-prem (PCI/PHI constraints for some customers), processing in public cloud for non-sensitive flows. They use Zendesk + homegrown routing.

Detailed points / quotes: 
- Peak behavior: typical baseline 1.2k rps, observed spikes to 3.5-4x baseline during campaigns; queue backpressure currently handled by degrading models (switch to small local NLU) which reduces quality.
- Desired outcome: keep agent suggestion latency consistent under spikes, avoid visible degradation of responses, and predictable unit economics. "We can tolerate lower-quality suggestions for low-priority tickets, but agent-facing suggestions must stay sub-200ms p95", said head of product.
- SLO targets: agent-suggest p95 <=120-200ms (channel dependent), end-to-end suggest + tool-call <=350ms; ticket-summary acceptable p95 <=750ms. Throughput target for POC: sustain 2.5k rps steady-state, tolerate 4k rps burst with graceful fallback.
- Architecture asks: dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, private control plane for data governance, VPC peering and option to run quantized model workers on-prem for PHI tenants. Prefers per-tenant model pinning and routing by cost/latency policies.
- Spike strategies they'd like to evaluate: pre-warming cache/KV for expected campaigns, burst autoscaling with warm standby nodes, automatic model-fanout (route to smaller quantized variant if cost tier triggers), token-level throttling with queue admission control, and prioritized request classes (CSAT-impacting tickets vs low-value).
- Tool-calling: deep integration with Zendesk and orchestration for 3rd-party tool calls (CRM writes, ticket merges). Need token rotation and scoped credentials for tool calls; want Redwood to support idempotent tool-call retries and structured function outputs.
- Security/compliance: strong requirement for SOC2 + KMS + detailed audit logging + log retention controls; data residency for EU-based enterprise customers.
- Cost sensitivity: estimates show 30-40% of infra cost is peak-driven; they want Optimize suggestions for quantization + batching to hit target ARR.
- POC plan (agreed): 4 weeks. Week1: load profile and metrics instrumentation (p95,p99,cost/ticket). Week2: dedicated capacity baseline, Week3: stress tests with synthetic bursts and seasonal campaign simulation, Week4: failure mode testing and runbook + SLA draft.
- Quotes: "If we can't keep suggest latency steady during a product launch, we lose CX and customers — need deterministic behavior", head of ops.
- Decisions pending: procurement sign-off for dedicated pool, legal sign-off on private control plane, and final network design (VPC peering or IPSEC).

Artifacts: Fireflies FF-20250201-2384, drive:/decks/Cascade_Redwood_POC_v1.pdf, internal infra stress report (attached to ticket SUP-1284).

Short-term next steps: Priya to send POC runbook and SLA template by 2025-02-20; security team to complete questionnaire by 2025-02-22.

Other notes: prefers concrete Fallback policies (A/B test) rather than opaque throttling; wants visibility into per-token cost during POC. Conversation style: lots of shorthand, action-oriented, engineering-first.
